cards.text: James calls himself a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ (James 1:1), and he's writing to believers he calls "my brothers." He just finished saying faith without deeds is dead (James 2:26). Now he's got a warning for anybody who wants to become a teacher.

cards.question: James says not many of his brothers should become teachers. Why?

answers.text: Teachers will be judged more strictly
Teachers will be paid too little

cards.text: Then James gets right in line with everybody: we all stumble in many ways. Friend, I once stamped FORTY cookies upside down and told the oven it was a new style.

cards.question: James says if anyone is never at fault in what he ___, he is a perfect man, able to control his whole body.

cards.text: Then James grabs a picture everybody knows: a big, strong horse, and a little bit people put in its mouth.

cards.question: When people put bits into horses' mouths to make them obey, what can they do?
Next James points to ships. They're huge, and strong winds drive them. What steers a ship wherever the pilot wants?
After the bit and the rudder, James turns to the tongue. True or false: he calls the tongue a small part of the body.
James says the tongue boasts of great things. Then he names another small thing with a huge result. What does he say a small spark can do?

cards.text: And James doesn't soften it one bit. The tongue is a fire, a world of wickedness among the parts of the body, and it is itself set on fire by hell.

cards.question: James says the tongue ___ the whole person and sets the course of his life on fire.

cards.text: Then James runs down the list: animals, birds, reptiles and sea creatures, all being tamed by people. Somebody out there tamed a REPTILE, friend, and I still can't get my oven timer to listen to me.

cards.question: True or false: James says people can tame the tongue the same way they tame animals.
James says no man can tame the tongue. How does he describe it?

answers.text: A restless evil full of deadly poison
A heavy burden full of bitter regret
A deep pit full of hidden traps

cards.text: Now James gets personal: with the tongue we bless our Lord and Father. Same tongue, same mouth, and then it turns right around and does something else.

cards.question: What else does James say we do with that same tongue we use to bless our Lord and Father?

answers.text: Curse people made in God's likeness
Lie to people who trust us

cards.question: Blessing and cursing come out of the same mouth. True or false: James says that's fine as long as there's more blessing than cursing.

cards.text: James wraps up with questions straight out of nature, starting with this one: "Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring?" Picture taking a big drink and getting a mouthful of OCEAN.

cards.question: James keeps going with trees and vines. True or false: he says a fig tree can grow olives.
James asks about the spring, the fig tree and the grapevine. What's he showing about blessing and cursing coming from the same mouth?
